Packaging claim: Store Barcodes Usually Identify Products, Not Prices
Core fact: A UPC carries a GTIN that identifies the product; the point-of-sale system uses that identity to look up price and inventory data.
Second reveal: That is why the same packaged product can have the same barcode but different prices at different stores or times.
First-frame and mechanism proof: Scan one familiar grocery barcode, then show the product ID lookup becoming a price on the register.
Search queries: UPC barcode grocery scan; supermarket checkout barcode; retail POS barcode
Fact boundaries: Say usually for standard UPC retail use. Do not claim no barcode format can ever encode price or other data.
